title: MA Protocol: Pre-Op and Post-Op
desc: Comprehensive pre-op and post-op MA checklists for FESS, septoplasty, and other surgical cases.

blocks.content: Pre-Op Appointment Checklist
EMR protocol
Apply the pre-op protocol in the EMR — there is a standard pre-op protocol template; use it as the starting point
Three required forms
Consent form — obtain and have the patient sign in clinic at this visit. Do NOT obtain for the first time on the day of surgery.
Medications form — document the prescriptions that will be issued: hydrocodone (pain management post-op) and ondansetron (nausea management post-op)
Patient health confirmation

Confirm the patient is feeling overall well — no fever, no active upper respiratory infection, no new illness since the last visit. If the patient is sick, alert the provider before proceeding — surgery may need to be postponed.
Confirm any current blood thinner medications — document name, dose, and when the patient last took it. The provider will advise on the hold protocol.
Confirm known sleep apnea — if yes, confirm whether the patient uses a CPAP and whether they will bring it to the surgery center
Standard medication management
ASA/NSAIDs: hold 7 days before surgery
Plavix: hold 5 days before surgery
NOACs: hold per drug-specific protocol — confirm with provider and PCP
Metformin: hold the day of surgery
Antihypertensives: continue with a small sip of water the morning of surgery
Insulin: adjusted for NPO status — patient's PCP or endocrinology advises
Herbal supplements: hold — garlic, ginkgo, fish oil, and St. John's wort all affect bleeding and anesthesia
Patient counseling
NPO after midnight — give written instructions. Some anesthesia groups allow clear liquids until 2 hours prior — confirm with the facility and specify in the instructions.
Responsible adult driver confirmed — not a rideshare; must be physically present at discharge
No jewelry, nail polish, or contact lenses on the day of surgery
No smoking — ideally 4+ weeks prior; minimum 24 hours before
Schedule the post-op follow-up appointment before the patient leaves today
Post-Op Visit Checklist
EMR protocol
Use the post-op protocol in the EMR — this charges only for post-op nasal endoscopy with debridement bilaterally. Do not charge a visit time code for post-op visits.
Patient check-in
Confirm whether the patient is currently on any prescription medication from the physician after surgery — particularly if FESS was performed

Check for any culture or MicroGen PCR results from the surgery — the physician may have collected intraoperative samples and results may be back; these guide post-surgical antibiotic selection. Flag any results for the provider before they enter the room.
Instrument setup
Always use the rigid scope — preferably the 30-degree scope for full sinus visualization in FESS patients
Set up: curved suction, size 8 and size 10 straight suctions, and plentiful 4×4 gauze for yourself, and a cup of water
For patients who underwent septoplasty: they typically have bilateral septal splints. Prepare iris scissors and a hemostat, and a small basin to catch the splint upon removal by the physician.
